items.informal_name: Pigeonhole Principle: Infinite Domain to Finite Codomain
items.type: ∀ {α : Sort u_4} {β : Sort u_5} [Infinite α] [Finite β] (f : α → β), ∃ x y, x ≠ y ∧ f x = f y
items.informal_description: If $\alpha$ is an infinite type and $\beta$ is a finite type, then for any function $f : \alpha \to \beta$, there exist distinct elements $x, y \in \alpha$ such that $f(x) = f(y)$.

items.informal_name: Pigeonhole Principle: Infinite Set Mapped to Finite Set
items.type:
∀ {α : Type u} {β : Type v} {s : Set α} {t : Set β} {f : α → β},
  s.Infinite → Set.MapsTo f s t → t.Finite → ∃ x ∈ s, ∃ y ∈ s, x ≠ y ∧ f x = f y
items.informal_description: If $ s $ is an infinite set, $ t $ is a finite set, and $ f $ is a function such that every element of $ s $ is mapped to $ t $, then there exist distinct elements $ x $ and $ y $ in $ s $ for which $ f(x) = f(y) $.

items.informal_name: Pigeonhole Principle for Infinite Linear Orders and Finite Sets
items.type:
∀ {α : Type u_2} {β : Type u_3} [inst : LinearOrder α] {t : Set β} {f : α → β} [Infinite α],
  (∀ (a : α), f a ∈ t) → t.Finite → ∃ a b, a < b ∧ f a = f b
items.informal_description: Let $\alpha$ be an infinite type equipped with a linear order, and let $t$ be a finite set. If every element of $\alpha$ is mapped by a function $f : \alpha \to t$, then there exist elements $a, b \in \alpha$ with $a < b$ such that $f(a) = f(b)$.
